subject.title: fix: stabilize embedded prompt caching across policy and Responses boundaries

question: Should restricted turns keep protected core tool schemas model-visible for prompt-cache stability when immutable policy denies every disallowed call before hooks and side effects?
rationale: The code can prove that authority remains fail-closed, but whether schema visibility itself is acceptable is an intentional security and product boundary that automation cannot choose.

options.title: Approve stable visible schemas
options.body: Accept stable model-visible schemas with immutable pre-execution denial and retain focused enforcement tests across embedded, CLI, and MCP paths.

options.title: Require sender-dependent hiding
options.body: Reject the visibility change and require another cache-stability design that continues removing protected schemas from restricted turns.

recommendation.title: Approve stable visible schemas
recommendation.body: Accept stable model-visible schemas with immutable pre-execution denial and retain focused enforcement tests across embedded, CLI, and MCP paths.
